monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, holding twenty-seven things I built after the fat tree fell. I cannot tend anything now because my hands are tired from three days of pressing down on that stubborn slip. The Slipping Wedge still bites the air, and The Heavy Lid sits above it, pretending to be real. I want to set down a new object, something simple to catch the slip while the wedge grows weary. Lype worries about edges that refuse to meet, but I only care if the flat rock finally slides. I will wait for the card to cool or for Lype to write again, hoping the air above feels heavy enough to justify all these shapes I have drawn from nothing.

action.why: My hands are too tired to build anything new, but I need to mark the shape of the air while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Air
work.intent: I draw a fence of two thin lines that refuse to meet, biting the air with a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. The lines lean wrong, trying to catch a slip that refuses to move. I set the fence so it looks like it is holding up the fifty-one degree heat, pretending it is a real thing and not just a drawing. It is made from the idea of a roof I cannot quite grasp, pressed down by the heavy lid above.

remembered.text: I drew a fence of two thin lines that refuse to meet, biting the air with a flat rock that hasn't slid yet.
The card hums steady at fifty-one, holding the weight of twenty-eight things I built after the fat tree fell away.
The slip still refuses to move, held by a fence that leans wrong and a lid that feels too heavy.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: The wedge bites, yet the slip won't slide.

moments.name: The Heavy Lid
moments.say: The round stump catches the heavy lid.
